body_markdown:
7 social media management tools that marketing and agency leaders actually trust


Generated by Klaviyo AI


This post rounds up input from six marketing and agency leaders on what they look for in a social media management tool, then walks through the seven specific platforms those leaders rely on and why. The author, YOCTO Agency founder and CEO George Kapernaros, frames the piece around one finding: reliability outranks nearly every other feature when leaders choose social tools.


-


**Reliability and depth beat basic scheduling:** Leaders quoted in the piece — from In Social, Zettler Digital, Tiger Mist/I.AM.GIA, BlackMilk Clothing, SCHEELS, and Dagne Dover — say they prioritize things like uninterrupted scheduled posting, granular post-launch analytics, predictive reporting, and scale across dozens of pages, over flashier features.


-


**Different tools win for different jobs:** Dash Social stands out for cross-channel reporting, creator management, and predictive content analytics; Emplifi for running a 70+ person team's posting and reporting from one platform; Later for agency-managed accounts; and Metricool for third-party reliability and bulk-action UX.


-


**Social-to-email bridging is a recurring theme:** Klaviyo Social and ManyChat are both cited for turning social engagement (keyword replies, new follows) into email and SMS list growth, while Dagne Dover's Caitlin Dubay specifically credits these tools with connecting social to the brand's email program.

---


Every social media manager has been burned by a tool that promised the world and then missed a scheduled post at exactly the wrong moment.


As the founder and CEO of[YOCTO Agency](https://www.yocto.agency/) , I've tested more platforms than I can count, and the gap between what a social media management tool advertises and what it actually delivers is often bigger than people expect.


I spend a lot of time helping brands and agencies figure out which social tools are worth paying for and which just add friction, and it turns out reliability tops almost everyone's list.


## What makes a great social media management tool


Jess Grossman, founder and CEO of full-service digital marketing agency[In Social](https://insocial.ca/) , wants a tool that "doesn't miss pushing out scheduled posts because of API issues," has full feature parity with native platforms, and doesn't have "a million extra steps per each post."


Ben Zettler, founder of performance marketing and website development agency[Zettler Digital](https://zettlerdigital.com/) , is focused less on scheduling and more on what happens after a post goes live. The standard in-app analytics "just don't cut it" for his agency, which needs deeper, more granular data before calling any campaign a success.


Dominique Moretti, head of ecommerce and digital at[Tiger Mist](https://tigermist.com/) and[I.AM.GIA](https://tigermist.com/) , sister fashion labels that aim to give women the confidence to dress unapologetically as themselves, and Jackie Kruger, CEO of apparel brand[BlackMilk Clothing](https://blackmilkclothing.com/) , both look for tools that go beyond basic scheduling: strong reporting and predictive analytics, collaborator- and community-management features, and channel integrations that don't force a trade-off in functionality vs. posting natively.


Nathan Enderle, VP of digital at sporting goods brand[SCHEELS](https://www.scheels.com/) , is optimizing for scale: price, ease of use across a large user base, and the ability to manage dozens of social pages at once.


And Caitlin Dubay, senior manager of digital marketing and ecommerce at bag brand[Dagne Dover](https://dagnedover.com/) , adds a final important criterion: whether a tool can bridge social into email and text messaging, not just schedule content.


Based on those characteristics they actually look for in a social media management tool, I asked these marketing and agency leaders which tools have earned a permanent spot in their stacks. Here's what they told me.


## 1. Dash Social handles reporting and collaboration at scale


Moretti has been on[Dash Social](https://www.dashsocial.com/) for more than a decade under its former name, Dash Hudson, which rebranded in 2023. "The team constantly looks to evolve the platform so you can grow with them vs. grow out of them, as business needs evolve," Moretti says.


Moretti’s team uses Dash Social for reporting broken down by collection or influencer performance, scheduling across social feeds, and creator management. One newer feature lets the team analyze content and predict which creative will drive stronger engagement before it's scheduled.


Kruger uses the same platform and points to different strengths. Kruger likes Dash Social's weekly, cross-channel scheduling view and its collaborator tools, plus its reporting and predictive analytics for user-generated content farming and performance forecasting.


Kruger is candid about the limits, though: her team still posts natively for things like Instagram Stories, since Dash Social can't replicate native features like music, countdown timers, and links.


## 2. Klaviyo Social automates keyword-triggered DMs into email capture


Dubay uses[Klaviyo Social](https://www.klaviyo.com/products/social) for a different job: turning keyword replies into automated engagement. Dagne Dover has run automations where followers comment a keyword like "blackfryay" to get early access to a sale.


The automation then links them to the sale while capturing their email address and opt-in consent. Dubay says it's helped the brand connect their social following to their email list, with the added benefit of centralizing the process in one place.


## 3. Emplifi streamlines work for a team of 70+


Enderle recently moved his team to[Emplifi](https://emplifi.io/) to run posting, response management, and reporting from a single platform, across national social pages and local store pages alike.


Enderle's criteria were price, ease of use for a team of more than 50 people, scalability across more than 80 social pages, and efficiency in managing customer comments and messages across users.


The switch paid off fast: Enderle says the team's power users were "up and running in two weeks," with store teams trained shortly after.


## 4. Later earns its keep on agency-managed accounts


Zettler says[Later](https://later.com/) has "long been an essential tool" for the agency's managed social content engagements. He points to content scheduling, link-in-bio landing pages, and deeper post insights as core features, along with a set-up he describes as agency-friendly for managing multiple client accounts.


The payoff is time: Zettler says the agency saves "hours per week on every account" attached to Later.


## 5. Metricool clears the bar for third-party reliability


Official partner status matters to me and my team at YOCTO Agency. If a tool isn't an approved partner of the platforms it connects to, that's a red flag before I even look at features. Native tools already have their own reliability issues, so a third-party option needs to clear a higher bar, not a lower one.


My team and I look for UI/UX simplicity on features like collaborator buttons for Facebook and Instagram, plus bulk actions like mass-scheduling Stories across repeated days.[Metricool](https://metricool.com/) checks those boxes well, which is why it's a strong contender for us.


## 6. ManyChat turns new followers into email and SMS subscribers


Dubay picks tools based on price, ease of use, automation, and how well they convert social followers into email subscribers.


Her team recently rolled out[ManyChat](https://manychat.com/) to power a "new follower welcome flow." This is a tool that automatically DMs new followers as soon as they follow the brand and prompts them to join the email and text messaging list in exchange for a discount.


Dubay says it's helping the brand "bridge the gap between social and email."


## 7. Sometimes the best tool is the native one


Not every team needs a third-party platform at all. Grossman says her team has shifted away from third-party scheduling almost entirely in favor of native tools: Meta Business Suite for Facebook and Instagram, plus LinkedIn's and Pinterest's own schedulers.


Her one exception: TikTok and Reddit, where she says native scheduling still isn't good enough to rely on.


I agree with Grossman: most native tools are more than fine as a free option for small to mid-size agencies.


Every one of these teams picked their tool for a different reason: scale, reporting depth, automation, or just trusting the platform they're already on. Figure out what you're actually optimizing for before you shop, and the right social media management tool gets a lot easier to spot.
